title: Hidden Twin Letters
kidRule: Some words hide twin letters that you cannot hear, like the two F's in GIRAFFE. Some hide two pairs of twins, like SUCCESS: two C's and then two S's. Champion spellers remember exactly which letters are twins and which letters stand alone.
hint: Twin letters are hiding in this word, and maybe more than one pair. Which letters come twice, side by side? Which ones stand alone?
reminder: Look for the twin letters. Think about which letter comes twice and which comes only once.

check.question: Why is SUCCESS tricky to spell?
check.correctAnswer: It hides two pairs of twin letters: two C's and then two S's!
distractors: Because it has a silent letter at the end
Because the letter U is never used in a long word

words.def: A very tall African animal with a long neck and a spotted coat.
words.sent: The giraffe nibbled leaves from the top of the tree.
words.story: A giraffe has only seven bones in its long neck. That is the same number you have in yours!
words.card: The *giraffe* won the *raff*le and got a very long scarf!

words.def: When something turns out the way you hoped.
words.sent: Our lemonade stand was a big success.
words.story: Thomas Edison and his team tested thousands of materials before they had success with a light bulb that kept glowing!
words.card: Re*cess* was a great *success*: we built a fort out of jackets!

words.def: As different as can be, like hot and cold, or on the other side.
words.sent: My best friend lives on the opposite side of the street.
words.story: The North Pole and the South Pole are on opposite ends of the Earth. When it is summer at one, it is winter at the other!
words.card: The frog h*opp*ed in the *opposite* direction and landed in the soup!

words.def: A sweet brown spice that is sprinkled on toast, rolls, and apples.
words.sent: Mom sprinkled cinnamon on my warm oatmeal.
words.story: Cinnamon is the inside bark of a tree! As the thin strips of bark dry, they curl up into little rolls.
words.card: The *inn* served *cinnamon* toast to every sleepy bear!

words.def: Needed; something you must have or do.
words.sent: A helmet is necessary when you ride your bike.
words.story: Spellers have a famous trick for this word: a shirt has one Collar and two Sleeves, so write one C and two S's!
words.card: It is *necessary* to wear a fancy dr*ess* to the worm's birthday!

words.def: To tell someone that something is good and worth trying.
words.sent: I recommend the strawberry ice cream.
words.story: This word is built from RE and COMMEND, an old word that means to praise. That is why it has one C and two M's!
words.card: I *recommend* that M*omm*y tries the spaghetti sundae!

words.sent: We baked a cake for the happy occasion.
words.story: This word comes from the Latin word 'occasio', which means a chance or just the right moment!
words.card: For this special *occasion*, the penguins played s*occ*er in bow ties!

words.story: Count the letters: four of the seven letters in this word are the letter S, in two pairs of twins!
words.card: The o*poss*um is proud to *possess* nine shiny buttons!

words.def: A group of people chosen to plan or decide something together.
words.sent: The party committee picked a dinosaur theme.
words.story: This word has three pairs of twin letters in a row of seven: two M's, two T's, and two E's!
words.card: The *committee* voted to wear one oven *mitt* each!

words.def: To have enough room for someone or something.
words.sent: Our car can accommodate seven people.
words.story: Spellers like to say that this word is roomy enough to hold two C's and two M's!
words.card: My lunchbox can *accommodate* nine trees of bro*cco*li!
